svg.text: Resume coherent state; measure both latency classes
Independent storage/commit and serial one-ms-per-position references
Checkpoint after all-layer success
At c3 retain valid KV and identity/credits
Next slice IDs13,14 at positions3,4
Partial candidate write does not publish c5
Short chunks keep accepted memory promises
Valid bytes384 → 640 → 896
Assigned bytes512 → 1024 → 1024
Two cap credits; final tail slack128 bytes
Whole prefill then three decode steps
P runs0–7; D outputs8,9,10 ms
P first output7; D gaps8,1,1 ms
Both requests drain at ten ms
Interleave chunks3/2/2 with decode
P runs0–3,4–6,7–9; D outputs4,7,10
P first output9; D gaps4,3,3 ms
Same serial work; different client experience
A logical in-memory checkpoint is not a durable file or proof of recovery after worker loss.
At P first-output ≤8 ms / D every gap ≤4 ms, neither serial schedule satisfies both.
